author: charlespips
text:
Hi ByTor,

Here is my view:

Here is the FLs on the left side:

In first chart, pink hollow boxes are supply FL, and light blue boxes are demand FL (except the top small box - it's just a QM zone). I highlight the green box (a demand FL) to let you know where it's broken, the lower green line is what really matter. When broken, it's looking for at least the clear demand zone just below it (I forgot to mark it). So after engulf, it's time to find the deepest retrace. first high is a good place to FO. Because I saw a nice QM level beforehand. and yes, price head down and FO directly into QM level and rejected nicely.

You'll need to figure out where is the FL is in order to read the correct ENG and FO. Hope it helps, any ideas are welcome

author: geejay
text:
@Tor: Have you ever done a study on how often a flag limit is engulfed, then there is a FO to the DP on the return?

Another question... have you tried examining the M30 chart for that trade. Would you buy based on M30? I have a tough time basing decisions on M5. I get decisions from higher time frame like M30 and H1. Then I look at M5 for entry opps and approaches to the target zones. But if I try to make decisions based on lower time frames, I tend to get slaughtered.

Those ideas are helping me have the patience to make better entries so I am on the right side of the market.

Btw, when I look at the chart from M30, I see a sell opp, not a buy. The FL was engulfed south, then price returned to what looks like the decision to engulf. Then it dropped to the origin. I don't have history lower than M30 so I cannot post a chart.

JC.

author: scoobydoo
text:
IF, thanks as usual for the trade explanations.

One thing I'm trying to properly understand is where the last set of orders reside. But the more I drill down the TFs the more I see... and the more I confuse myself!

Price doesn't quite return to the LS of the QM and I know from your webinar that it certainly doesn't have to be exact, but I still need to pinpoint a sell point. On the 5 min chart it looks like price is nicely CP right above where you sell so it looks like a great entry. But when we go down to the 1 min chart the CP isn't so obvious.

Of course, when we drill down into fractals there are decisions within the larger decisions. The green box is a failed bullish QM which quite often finds a nice reaction on return. But, I can also see the trick played at the green box - there's a nice push down out of the range followed by a nice push up so I guess the blue box is also the last decision made before we drop out of this range and the blue box is also the first FTR after the last push up in price. The sell line has a few nice SR rejections from it on 1 min but not so obvious in 5 min.

I'd be very grateful if you could give me any hints as to where I'm going wrong at the moment. I feel I'm just seeing to much and I'm not properly focusing on the most important stuff.

author: Ifmyante
text:
Please remember, RTM is a puzzle. I've given you every piece, and have even put most of the pieces together for you.

If I put the rest of the pieces together, here, publicly, soon enough the picture will change, and the pieces will mutate to no longer fit as they did.

This would benefit nobody.

To be frank, it has baffled me how not every member of RTM is a Master Trader already, but I have to realise that there are greater obstacles than an incomplete understanding of how the market works. We all have our inner daemons, working for or against us, which must be nurtured or banished for us to succeed.

Identify these daemons and deal with them, and you'll never need another hint!
